==Problem 2 ==
What is the value of this expression in decimal form?

 <cmath>\frac{44}{11} + \frac{110}{44} + \frac{44}{1100}</cmath>
<imath>\textbf{(A) } 6.4\qquad\textbf{(B) } 6.504\qquad\textbf{(C) } 6.54\qquad\textbf{(D) } 6.9\qquad\textbf{(E) } 6.94</imath>

==Solution 1== 

We see that <imath>\frac{44}{11}</imath> is <imath>4</imath>; 
<imath>\frac{110}{44}</imath> simplifies to <imath>\frac{5}{2}</imath>, which is <imath>2.5</imath>; 

and <imath>\frac{44}{1100}</imath> simplifies to <imath>\frac{1}{25}</imath>, which is <imath>0.04</imath>; 

<imath>4+2.5+0.04</imath> reveals <cmath>\frac{44}{11} + \frac{110}{44} + \frac{44}{1100}</cmath> is <imath>\boxed{\text{(C)\ 6.54}}</imath>. 
~ 

~Minor Formatting by GreenPlanet2050

==Solution 2 (not recommended)==

Using brute force we can make <imath>\frac{44}{11}</imath> into <imath>\frac{4400}{1100}</imath>, <imath>\frac{110}{44}</imath> into <imath>\frac{2750}{1100}</imath>, and <imath>\frac{44}{1100}</imath>, and then we add and get <imath>\frac{7194}{1100}</imath> and this simplifies to <imath>\boxed{\text{(C)\ 6.54}}</imath>

~VersatileGopher38
